page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n4.large is an entry-level virtual machine instance within the ecs.n4 server family. It is built on the KVM hypervisor and runs on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration features an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz, providing 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU allocation is shared, which introduces potential resource contention. It is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. No local storage or dedicated GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 0 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the ecs.n4.large operates in the lower tiers of performance. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is measured at 1107.98, placing it in the bottom 25%, while multi-core performance drops to the bottom 10% with a score of 2199.5. Memory bandwidth tests show a similar trend, with uncached large-block read speeds at 17.08 GB/sec and write speeds at 14.55 GB/sec. Computational workloads such as software compilation with clang and image processing fall into the bottom 10% of tested servers. The shared CPU allocation and lack of baseline network bandwidth represent significant performance tradeoffs.

Given its shared CPU model and modest resource allocation, this instance is positioned as a budget-friendly option for non-critical workloads. It is suitable for low-traffic static web serving, basic text processing, and lightweight development or testing environments. It is not designed for database operations, large-scale LLM inference, or memory-intensive applications, as demonstrated by its low passmark database score of 565.0 and poor multi-core performance.
